label: <DEL> step in long sequences (L=8-9), content-gated
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (85% of activation mass) plus a weaker tail on the first one or two copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, about 15% of mass). It never fires in the original phase. It is strongly length-dependent: L=9 holds 71% of mass and L=8 holds 25%, and it is essentially silent for L<=6. Even at <DEL> with L>=8, only about 29% of steps are active, so firing also depends on sequence content. Precision improves somewhat when many of {u,k,p,b,d,h,f,w} appear in the prefix, or when the first token is one of {v,y,t,c,3,q,j,e,g,n}; top examples often begin with v, c or g. But a predicate built on these sets only raised dev F1 from 0.42 to 0.49, so the content dependence is distributed rather than a clean rule. The strongest activations come at <DEL> in L=9 sequences, followed by smaller activations on the first copy output. Dev score for (phase==1)&(L>=8): P 0.29, R 0.74, mass recall 0.83.
